domain: wildfire operations - initial-attack escape and containment-duration prediction from the regulator's assessment record (per-incident classification, Alberta Forest Protection Area 2006-2025)
prediction_question: At Alberta Wildfire's recorded initial assessment of a newly discovered wildfire (assessment_datetime, 'originally assessed'), predict whether the wildfire will escape initial attack - final area burned at least 100 ha (variants at 4/40/200 ha) - and/or remain uncontained more than 72 hours (time from assessment to first under control), using only the crew-observed assessment record (size at assessment, rate of spread, fire behaviour type, position on slope, in-situ weather over the fire, FBP fuel type), pre-instant timing fields (estimated ignition, reported, detection channel), and calendar/geography. A useful prediction supports the actual initial-attack resourcing decision - airtanker/crew prioritization and same-day escalation - which the agency itself states happens at this instant.
prediction_time: The initial assessment instant, assessment_datetime, documented by the publisher as 'the date and time the wildfire was originally assessed by Alberta Wildfire employees'. Every feature field's meaning is documented at that instant: assessment_hectares, fire_spread_rate, fire_type, fire_position_on_slope, the five in-situ weather fields and fuel_type all carry the publisher's wording 'at the time of initial assessment'; reported_date/discovered_date/fire_start_date/detection fields are documented pre-instant and measured never to fall after the instant (27,828/27,828 for reported_date). Post-instant families are excluded by design and measurement: cause classification (dictionary: 'under investigation' temporary cause, final cause updated later), dispatch block (2.41% of dispatch timestamps fall after the assessment - mixed ordering, so excluded), all suppression/milestone fields (initial_action_by, ia_*, fire_fighting_start_*, bucketing, first_bh/uc/to/ex) and the label sources (current_size, size_class). Timestamps carry no timezone; they are read as local Alberta operational time (America/Edmonton) - a declared assumption to be confirmed at construction and stated in quality.json.evaluation_contract.
target_definition: Primary label, binary: escape = final area burned (current_size, the publisher's 'final area burned of the wildfire') at or above the threshold (primary 100 ha; variants 4/40/200 ha measured). Secondary label, binary: containment = first under control (first_uc_date, 'sufficient suppression action to ensure no further spread') later than 72 hours after assessment_datetime; 42.0% of fires were already under control at the assessment instant (assessment == first_uc, a degenerate label-0 stratum the construction decision must handle and declare). Both labels derive entirely from the record's own post-instant fields; both source columns are excludable from what ships. Population: all wildfires in Alberta's Forest Protection Area, 2006-2025, one row per wildfire ((YEAR, FIRE_NUMBER) unique, measured); eligibility is assessment-based, not outcome-based (100% of discovered wildfires are assessed).

Licence text read 2026-11-06 from https://open.alberta.ca/licence (Open Government Licence - Alberta, version 2.2): 'The Information Provider grants you a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use the Information, including for commercial purposes, subject to the terms below.' / 'You are free to: Copy, modify, publish, translate, adapt, distribute or otherwise use the Information in any medium, mode or format for any lawful purpose.' / 'You must, where you do any of the above: Acknowledge the source of the Information by including any attribution statement specified by the Information Provider(s) and, where possible, provide a link to this licence.' / default attribution: 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Alberta.' / 'This licence does not grant you any right to use the Information in a way that suggests any official status or that the Information Provider endorses you or your use of the Information.' / exemptions include 'Personal Information'. The attribution sentence is carried verbatim into LICENSE.md at packaging; the non-endorsement clause is satisfied by derived-work labeling.

Personal-information exemption verified not engaged by the shipped columns (measured 2026-11-06): assessment_resource carries 5 position categories (IA Forces 23,170 / Other 2,741 / Wildfire Assessor 1,091 / AAO 825 / blank 1), dispatched_resource and initial_action_by carry resource-type codes - no person names in any shipped column (the dictionary's prose describes the operational form; the published CSV carries positions).
No third-party rights engaged: the record is the Government of Alberta's own operational wildfire compilation (publisher: Forestry and Parks / Alberta Wildfire).
licence_note: Open Government Licence - Alberta v2.2 permits redistribution, adaptation and commercial use; the binding condition is attribution ('Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Alberta.' plus a licence link) - recorded and carried into LICENSE.md verbatim at packaging, per the tick's standing warning about OGL attribution terms. Non-endorsement clause: the dataset card and README must label the work as derived and never as Alberta Wildfire's official product.
split_strategy: Temporal, disjoint by year: train 2006-2015 (15,944 fires), eval 2016-2020 (5,627), holdout 2021-2025 (6,257). Measured positives, primary escape label >= 100 ha: train 297 (1.86%), eval 104 (1.85%), holdout 257 (4.11%); containment > 72 h: 514 (3.2%), 189 (3.4%), 611 (9.8%). Both classes present in every window at every measured threshold (4/10/40/100/200/1000 ha). Positives cluster on extreme-weather days: distinct assessment dates of >=100 ha positives are 156/79/128 per window - report clustered counts and score with day-cluster awareness. The holdout escape rate is higher because 2021-2025 contains the 2023 record season - real, documented non-stationarity (see known-event fixtures in notes.md), not a construction defect.

measurements.rows_and_uniqueness: 27,828 wildfires 2006-2025; (YEAR, FIRE_NUMBER) unique (0 duplicates); 0 unparseable timestamps; 0 current_size=0 rows; 0 size-class/current-size inconsistencies (A>=0-0.1, B>0.1-4, C>4-40, D>40-200, E>200 ha).
measurements.instant_ordering: assessment_datetime never precedes reported_date (27,828/27,828), discovered_date (21,977/21,977) or fire_start_date (27,109/27,109); dispatch_date falls after assessment for 670/27,813 (2.41%) and start_for_fire_date for 990/27,818 (3.56%) - dispatch block excluded from features on this mixed ordering evidence.
measurements.feature_coverage_by_window: assessment_datetime/assessment_hectares 100% in all windows; weather block (temperature, relative_humidity, wind_speed, wind_direction, weather_conditions_over_fire) 88.8%/86.4%/94.0%; fire_spread_rate 88.9%/86.7%/94.6%; fuel_type 68.8%/71.1%/81.6%; fire_type 89.2%/88.0%/96.0%; reported_date 100%; discovered_date 88.8%/72.4%/59.9% (dictionary: blank where unplanned detection); fire_start_date ~97.4% throughout.
measurements.escape_base_rates: >=100 ha: 297/104/257 (1.86%/1.85%/4.11%); >=200 ha: 235/76/217; >=4 ha: 1,167/433/705; full threshold table in probe_escape_base_rates_result.json with distinct-date clustered counts.
measurements.containment_duration: assessment -> first under control: median 0.4 h, p90 24.4 h, >72 h for 4.72% overall (514/189/611 per window); 11,688/27,828 (42.0%) already under control at the assessment instant.
measurements.publisher_cross_check: current CSV hectares vs published season totals: 2020 3,274 vs 3,269; 2021 54,089 vs 54,047; 2022 131,272 vs 130,858; 2023 2,217,295 vs 2,211,900; 2024 714,874 vs 708,528 (<=1.0%); 2019 791,838 vs 883,411 (-10.4%), consistent with the dictionary's documented spring aerial-photography revision; fire counts differ from season PDFs because the CSV is year-round (e.g. 31 winter wildfires Nov-Dec 2025).
measurements.revision_sensitivity: fires within +-20% of the 100 ha threshold: 89 (0.32% of rows); 40 ha: 146; 10 ha: 260; 4 ha: 383 - bounds the post-hoc area-revision label-flip exposure.
measurements.provenance_mix: detection channel drifts (lookouts 34% of 2006 -> 21% of 2025; unplanned 42% -> 59%); population definition (all FPA wildfires) is stable; full per-year mixes in probe result JSON.
measurements.vintage_limitation: single current compilation (portal updated 2026-02-17, covers through 2025); per-fire historical vintages are not published and not recoverable; the dictionary documents in-place revision of area burned (spring aerial-photography interpretation), cause (under-investigation -> final) and location (assessment GPS -> confirmed ignition area); the 2019 aggregate revision measured above is direct evidence. The task is therefore a current-compilation retrospective with explicit evaluation_contract assumptions - it does not claim operational point-in-time reproducibility of historical values.
measurements.extraction_cost_measured: one 10.4 MB CSV + one 193 KB dictionary PDF through the cleared browser context (~12 s transfer, ~25 s chunked export) on the coordinator container (4 vCPU); full-population probes run in ~3 s locally; construction is a single 10.4 MB parse on a worker. No bulk transfer beyond the source file.
measurements.access_caveat: open.alberta.ca blocks plain HTTP clients (Cloudflare managed challenge, measured); construction must ship the sha256-pinned CSV in the job bundle or use the recorded browser procedure, and assert the digest in-build.

review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (probes and full transcripts in candidates/ab-wildfire-ia-escape/). (1) Redistribution: class A - OGL-Alberta v2.2 permits redistribution and derivatives; the attribution sentence and non-endorsement wording are recorded verbatim and carried into LICENSE.md; the personal-information exemption was checked against the shipped columns (position codes, not names). (2) Prediction timing: the instant is the publisher's own initial-assessment timestamp and every intended feature is documented 'at the time of initial assessment' by the publisher's dictionary - the strongest timing documentation of any source this bench has opened; post-instant families (cause, dispatch, suppression milestones) are excluded with measured ordering evidence; declared limitations: no timezone marker in timestamps (read as America/Edmonton, assumption to confirm) and a single current compilation (no historical per-fire vintages) - the task is labelled current-compilation retrospective, and evaluation_contract must state these assumptions plus the bounded revision-flip exposure (89 fires within +-20% of 100 ha). (3) Target: labels derive from the record's own post-instant fields (current_size, first_uc_date), excludable from shipped features; eligibility is assessment-based with 100% coverage - no outcome-conditioned selection; no censoring (terminal status on every row, 99.9% extinguished). (4) Split capacity: three disjoint year windows carry both classes for both labels (escape 1.86%/1.85%/4.11%; containment 3.2%/3.4%/9.8%), with same-day clustered counts recorded (independence scale = the extreme fire-weather day); the holdout's higher rate is the documented 2023 record season. (5) Not a mirror: the IA-escape family is precedented (WildfireIA US benchmark, Mesogeos, Zong et al. Alberta powerline subset, Korkola et al. Ontario, UAlberta IA-difficulty study) - none ships an all-cause, assessment-instant task on the regulator's own in-situ assessment observations with containment-milestone labels; WildfireIA's own abstract records that such 'response records' are non-public in the US, which is precisely the gap this source closes for a public jurisdiction. Novelty verdict 'differentiated' recorded by script. Residual uncertainties for construction: confirm the timezone reading against a publicly documented fire timeline; decide the already-controlled stratum's treatment for the containment label; winter/season scope decision.
next_action: Hand to construction (worker, advancement session): (1) acquire the CSV via bundle-shipped pinned copy or the recorded browser procedure and assert sha256 8b6ed447... in-build; (2) population = all assessed FPA wildfires 2006-2025 (decide winter-row scope once and declare); (3) primary label escape (final >= 100 ha), secondary containment (> 72 h to first under control, with an explicit decision on the 42% already-controlled-at-assessment stratum); (4) features = the assessment block + pre-instant timing/detection + calendar/geography; exclude cause-family, dispatch block, suppression/milestone fields and label sources - enforce this column policy in code, not convention; (5) confirm the America/Edmonton timezone reading against a publicly documented fire timeline (e.g. Horse River 2016) and declare it in quality.json.evaluation_contract; (6) splits train 2006-2015 / eval 2016-2020 / holdout 2021-2025; document the 2023-season base-rate shift in the card; (7) assert known-event fixtures in-build (Richardson 2011, Horse River 2016, Chuckegg Creek 2019, Basset/Long Lake/Pembina 2023 at the publisher's own final sizes; LWF002 2023 as an already-controlled negative); (8) gate 1.5 evaluation_contract with the current-compilation retrospective scope, the vintage limitations and the bounded revision-flip exposure; run the reverse-history join probes on the exact artifact; (9) full-worker qualification -> exact-byte acceptance -> baseline triad before any AUC/base-rate/headroom figure is quoted; (10) LICENSE.md: MIT for our code, CC0 for our compilation rights, Alberta's attribution sentence verbatim, derived-not-official labeling per the non-endorsement clause.

novelty_check.theirs: WildfireIA (arXiv 2606.15529, 2026) is a US national IA-failure benchmark but from discovery-time public geodata (FIRMS/VIIRS, gridMET, LANDFIRE, OSM, WorldPop) for naturally-caused FPA-FOD fires, excludes containment timestamps, and its own abstract records that operational response records are non-public; Mesogeos (NeurIPS 2023) ships Mediterranean ignition-point burned-area estimation from environmental covariates; Zong, Xianli & Flannigan (Earth's Future 2026, Zenodo 21845674) ship only the powerline-caused Alberta subset (294 kB CSV) with weather/topography covariates and an ignition-day 2 ha escape rule - not the assessment instant and not all causes; Korkola et al. (IJWF 2024) model Ontario IA success on non-public Ontario fire reports; the UAlberta initial-attack-difficulty study (2023) uses 15 years of Alberta data in a simulation and publishes no task; ABNextFire ships Alberta Landsat spread grids, not escape records
novelty_check.ours: All-cause Alberta Forest Protection Area per-wildfire task at the publisher-documented initial-assessment instant (27,828 fires, 2006-2025) whose features are the regulator's own crew-observed assessment record (assessment size, rate of spread, fire behaviour, position on slope, in-situ weather over the fire, FBP fuel type, detection channel), with a final-area escape label and a time-to-under-control containment label, temporal splits and a publisher-cross-checked revision record; no public source ships in-situ initial-attack assessment observations at per-incident grain for any jurisdiction, and no Alberta all-cause assessment-instant escape task exists in ML-ready form
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
